dedupe_keys.name: fao desert locust watch desert locust information service

description: FAO Desert Locust Watch is the hub of FAO's Desert Locust Information Service (DLIS), which monitors the global desert locust situation around the clock and issues monthly bulletins with country-by-country forecasts of migration and breeding, forecasts up to six weeks ahead, and ad hoc alerts and warnings on the timing, scale and location of invasions. It is run by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, which combines locust survey data sent by affected countries with weather, habitat and satellite imagery. Coverage is about 30 countries in Africa, the Near East and South-West Asia, some 16 million square kilometres during recession periods; during the 2020 to 2021 upsurge in Eastern Africa, South-West Asia and the Red Sea region FAO made the response one of its highest corporate priorities. Bulletins, forecasts and maps are available free online as PDF documents and maps; the page read states no licence. Caveats: products are expert assessments built on national survey reports, whose completeness drops in insecure or remote areas. For simulation it gives pest hazard occurrence and forecasts for crop exposure and emergency response models of food supply in the affected regions. It is related to the Global Dataset of Historical Yields record in this catalogue, which can show the yield effects of such outbreaks.
